title: Sablewood Route Gate
kicker: The road crossing where nature, signage, and corporate language first collide.
hook: The road crossing where nature, signage, and corporate language first collide.

blocks.label: Arrival Read
blocks.body: The route gate is where polished assurance meets wet bark, old stone, and a forest that has not signed anything.

blocks.label: Known For
blocks.body: A tiny official station tries to draw straight lines across a forest that only does curves. Roots have buckled the queue-stones into a slow stone wave. Vines steal loose paper off the desk overnight. The inspection counter is a cut stump the size of a wagon...

blocks.label: What Is Here
blocks.body: Local residents or workers appropriate to the place fox-bats nest above the stamp shed small root mice chew wax seals lark-moths orbit lanterns during delays No default combatant; add only if the scene introduces one Local civic, trade, or route interests...

blocks.label: Food And Texture
blocks.body: A cheap stall fries dough in forest fat while you wait, and a man with a confident smile sells ward-tokens of deeply uncertain power. The coffee is bitter and free if you look official enough to be worth the favor.

affordances: Look for the busiest local gathering point.
